blocks.x: How Cyber & Zero-Trust lands in Medical Devices & MedTech — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

MedTech sells outcomes and must prove them: connected devices generate telemetry that feeds service revenue, clinical evidence and regulatory post-market surveillance. The device-to-evidence loop is an engineering product — and EU MDR/CRA raise its bar.

items: EU CRA/MDR cybersecurity duties land on fleets with legacy firmware; SBOMs unknown.
Installed base lacks provisioning/OTA; service runs on reactive dispatch and field guesswork.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, AI Security & Model Protection, Cyber Resilience & Incident Recovery from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Device provisioning/OTA, Service dispatch, Vigilance reporting) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — EU MDR among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Evidence once, audit anywhere: compliance automation across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA and privacy.
Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
SBOMs, signed firmware and vulnerability SLAs (CRA/MDR duties evidenced)

blocks.caption: Regimes shaping this capability
rows: PHI safeguards, BAAs, breach notification and audit trails

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Healthcare & Life Sciences level this capability reads as: IEC 80001-informed zoning for legacy devices with monitoring (unmanaged device surface made visible and controlled). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline with your team: the current metric is measured, signed and stored as the reference for every later gate. Weeks 3–8 run the pilot on deliberately narrow scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, never quietly extended.
